evidence: The n-parameter mass recurrence and testing argument check out. From m_r=theta S_r, the cutoff theta(D+1)^(n-1)<=1/4 gives coordinate growth S_{r+e_i}<=4S_r/3. The anchored A_p sum is dominated by a product-geometric series with ratio 2^{-p}(4/3)^{p-1}<1, while a two-cell rectangle gives the matching theta^{1-p} lower characteristic. On the hyperbolic region theta*prod(r_i+1)<=1/2 one has S_r<=2; its divisor-type cardinality is of order at least theta^{-1} log^{n-1}(1/theta). The source-cell test therefore gives the claimed theta^{-1} log^{(n-1)/p}(1/theta) operator lower bound. The coordinatewise averaging/reflection step is compatible with both the weight and dual weight because the comparison interval depends only on geometry.

evidence: The novelty survives after narrowing it to the dimension-amplified n>=3 statement. Lerner supplies only the planar p=2 obstruction. Earlier SCOPE record `all-p-logarithmic-obstruction-strong-maximal--cec7237f693b` already gives the all-p lower factor (log A)^{1/p} in every dimension by embedding the planar construction, and `tensor-amplification-strong-maximal-a2-obstruction--dfc5a7d88a20` gives the p=2 tensor exponent floor(n/2)/2. The assigned direct n-parameter construction instead yields (n-1)/p, which is strictly stronger for n>=3 (and at p=2 improves the pairwise tensor exponent). The n=2 portion is not separately novel and is excluded from the originality claim.

The direct n-parameter construction reveals a genuine dimension-amplified logarithmic obstruction rather than merely propagating the planar result. It strengthens the known lower logarithmic exponent in higher dimension while leaving the open optimal power problem untouched, so it is a meaningful quantitative advance.
